result.title: E2SIM: Long-Horizon Simulation of Everyday Human Behavior with Evolving States
result.summary: AI agents are increasingly expected to support users over long periods, across work, and daily life. This requires modeling not only who users are, but also how their goals, interests, activities, and interactions evolve over time. A challenge in longitudinal user simulation is maintaining consistency between these evolving states and the consequences of actions in a shared environment. We introduce E2SIM, a longitudinal user simulation framework that jointly models evolving actor states and a dynamic shared environment. E2SIM connects actor-state updates with shared-world changes through a feedback loop linking immediate actions, delayed outcomes, and actor-specific observations across work and life. This allows the consequences of earlier actions to shape later behavior, while preserving differences in what each actor knows. We further propose a suite of longitudinal trajectory diagnostics, measuring dynamic consistency, coherent event progression and collaboration, and non-degenerate trajectory development rather than static consistency alone. In one 60-day simulation, E2SIM produced more extracted event threads judged meaningful by our evaluator and fewer near-duplicate actions than four direct-generation baselines. The framework and evaluation methods provide a basis for studying longitudinal user simulation, with potential applications in training and evaluating AI agents that assist users over extended periods.

AI.brief_summary: E2SIM 是一个长时段用户行为模拟框架，把行为者内部状态的演化与共享环境的动态变化用「即时行动—延迟结果—个体特异观测」的反馈回路耦合起来，并提出一套衡量长程轨迹动态一致性与事件推进的诊断指标。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「个体特异观测」与状态、世界更新相互制约的设计，可能为 LVR 中部分可观测下的信念状态维护、以及 latent 状态长程漂移的评价提供概念线索；但论文不含视觉或多模态推理，借鉴需较多核查。
